The supply of printed books by Satyamev Printers constitutes a **composite supply** under Section 2(30) of the CGST Act, 2017, where the principal supply is the supply of goods (printed books). 

As per the principle of "naturally bundled" services, the supply of paper and printing services is ancillary to the delivery of the final printed book. Under Section 8(a) of the CGST Act, the tax liability on a composite supply shall be determined by the rate applicable to the principal supply. Since the principal supply is the printed book (goods), the GST rate applicable to goods, i.e., **12%**, shall apply to the entire transaction. This is further supported by the classification of printed books under HSN 4901.
ec31281d6f0210ab359efed564ec8f51c9dc620b:
The view taken by XYZ Consultancy is **invalid in law**.

Under **Section 7(1)(a)** of the CGST Act, 2017, the scope of "supply" includes all forms of supply of goods or services for a consideration. Furthermore, **Paragraph 5(e) of Schedule II** explicitly classifies "agreeing to the obligation to refrain from an act, or to tolerate an act or a situation, or to do an act" as a supply of service.

The payment of ₹37 lakh received for a non-compete agreement constitutes a consideration for the supply of services by way of "tolerating an act" or "refraining from an act." Consequently, this transaction is taxable under GST. The fact that the consideration is inclusive of tax does not exempt the supply from the levy.

As per **Section 12(7)(a) of the IGST Act, 2017**, the place of supply of services provided by way of organization of an event to a registered person shall be the location of such person.

In the first scenario, since Damani Industries is registered in Mumbai, the place of supply is **Mumbai (Maharashtra)**, regardless of the event being held in Bangalore.

In the second scenario, where the event is organized in Dubai, the place of supply is determined under **Section 13(5) of the IGST Act, 2017**. Since the event is held outside India, the place of supply shall be the **place where the event is actually held**, which is **Dubai**. Consequently, this transaction qualifies as an export of services, provided other conditions under Section 2(6) are met.
f84f6ce16efcc853aa999cf7d7f0552c216b1599:
The services provided by ABC Pvt. Ltd. qualify as an **"Export of Service"** under **Section 2(6) of the IGST Act, 2017**, provided all conditions are satisfied.

The activity constitutes a supply of services where the supplier is in India, the recipient is outside India, and the place of supply is outside India (determined under **Section 13(2) of the IGST Act** as the location of the recipient). Crucially, the payment is received in convertible foreign exchange, and the supplier and recipient are not merely establishments of a distinct person. 

Since ABC Pvt. Ltd. acts as an intermediary/facilitator and not as an agent for the transaction of goods, the service is not excluded under the "Intermediary" definition, provided the conditions of **Section 2(13)** are not met.

The view taken by Vedanta Hospital is partially incorrect. 

Under **Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate)**, health care services provided by a clinical establishment are exempt. As per the **CBIC Circular No. 32/6/2018-GST**, food supplied to in-patients as advised by doctors/nutritionists is considered a part of the composite supply of health care services and is exempt.

However, food supplied to out-patients, attendants, or visitors does not qualify as a health care service. Such supplies are independent transactions and are taxable as "restaurant services" under **Section 9(1)** of the CGST Act. Therefore, while the supply to in-patients is exempt, the supply to non-admitted persons is liable to GST at the applicable rates, and the hospital’s claim of total exemption is legally untenable.

As per **Section 12(1)** of the **CGST Act, 2017**, the time of supply of goods shall be the earlier of the dates specified under **Section 12(2)**.

For the supply of goods, the time of supply is the earlier of:
1. The date of issue of invoice by the supplier or the last date on which he is required to issue the invoice under **Section 31(1)**.
2. The date on which the supplier receives the payment.

In the present case, the invoice was issued on 25th June. As per **Notification No. 66/2017–Central Tax**, the requirement to pay tax on advances received for the supply of goods has been waived. Thus, the time of supply is the date of invoice, i.e., **25th June**.

As per Section 22 of the CGST Act, 2017, a supplier is liable to be registered if their aggregate turnover exceeds the threshold limit (₹20 lakh for Tamil Nadu). Although product 'X' was exempt, the exemption was withdrawn on 1st November. Aggregate turnover includes the value of exempt supplies. The provisions under the CGST Act, 2017 are as follows:

**(i) Advance Payment (No Supply):** As per **Section 31(3)(e)**, where an advance is received but no supply is subsequently made, the registered person must issue a **Receipt Voucher**. Upon cancellation of the supply, a **Refund Voucher** must be issued under **Section 31(3)(f)** to the person who made the payment.

**(ii) Goods on Approval:** Under **Section 31(7)**, where goods are sent on approval for sale or return, the invoice must be issued either at the time of supply or six months from the date of removal, whichever is earlier.

**(iii) Continuous Supply of Services:** Per **Section 31(5)(b)**, where the due date is not ascertainable, the invoice must be issued before or at the time when the supplier receives the payment.

7c16db139ef6f7308b113ace9144bcc05ee534d5:
Under the provisions of the **CGST Act, 2017**, Input Tax Credit (ITC) cannot be utilized for the payment of interest, penalty, or tax payable under the Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM).

**Section 49(4)** of the CGST Act stipulates that the amount available in the electronic credit ledger may be used for making payment towards **output tax** only. Since RCM liability is not considered "output tax" (as defined under **Section 2(82)**), it must be discharged in cash via the electronic cash ledger. Similarly, interest and penalties are statutory levies distinct from output tax liability and are not covered under the scope of ITC utilization. Consequently, these liabilities must be settled exclusively through cash payments under **Section 49(3)**.

    *   Own Sale (Mobile): ₹30,000. IGST @ 18% = ₹5,400.

3d8fc9ff8af9ba64ecae9821d8225f53467430d2:
Under Section 52 of the CGST Act, 2017, every Electronic Commerce Operator (ECO) is mandated to collect Tax Collected at Source (TCS) on the net value of taxable supplies made through it by other suppliers, where the consideration is collected by the ECO.

However, this requirement is subject to specific exceptions. Per Notification No. 12/2018-Central Tax, ECOs are exempt from TCS obligations if they are liable to pay tax under Section 9(5) of the CGST Act (e.g., passenger transport, restaurant services, or housekeeping services provided through the ECO). Furthermore, if the supplier is exempt from registration under Section 23, the ECO is not required to collect TCS. Thus, while the general rule mandates TCS, it applies only to taxable supplies where the ECO facilitates payment.
3dfae65bdc89d5de28f1070e781ad3a8cc5be2dc:
Under Section 9(5) of the CGST Act, 2017, the government may specify categories of services where the tax on intra-state supplies shall be paid by the electronic commerce operator (ECO) as if the operator were the supplier. 

Notification No. 17/2017-Central Tax (Rate) specifies "housekeeping services" as a category of service where the ECO is liable to pay GST. Consequently, Hi-Tech Indya Pvt. Ltd. is mandatorily liable to pay GST on the housekeeping services supplied through its platform, regardless of the turnover of the actual service provider, AB Pvt. Ltd. 

Furthermore, as per Section 24(ix) of the CGST Act, persons who are required to pay tax under Section 9(5) are required to obtain compulsory registration. Thus, Hi-Tech Indya Pvt. Ltd. must register and discharge the GST liability.
c2af10ac2f03aa4dd7e13f1b84cac3ed33540b67:
Under the GST law, the taxability of the Securities Lending Scheme, 1997, is governed by **Entry 27(a) of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate)**. 

The lending of securities under the Securities Lending Scheme, 1997, is considered a "service" by way of extending deposits, loans, or advances in so far as the consideration is represented by way of interest or discount. However, for the purpose of GST, the lending fee charged by the intermediary is treated as consideration for the service of facilitating the lending of securities. 

As per the **Securities Lending Scheme, 1997**, the lending fee is taxable under the **Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM)** as per **Notification No. 22/2017-Central Tax (Rate)**, where the borrower (Dhandhan Bank) is liable to pay GST.

The taxability of the supplies is determined as follows:

(i) **Laptop and bag:** This is a **mixed supply** under Section 2(74) of the CGST Act, as they are not naturally bundled. Per Section 8(b), the tax rate applicable is the highest rate, i.e., **28%**.

(ii) **Kits:** This is a **composite supply** under Section 2(30). As the hair oil is the principal supply, the rate applicable is **18%**.

(iii) **Free gifts:** As per Schedule I, gifts to unrelated persons are not "supply" for lack of consideration. No GST is applicable.

(iv) **Event management:** Services provided free to a relative are not "supply" under Section 7(1)(c) as they lack consideration and are not in the course of business.

(v) **Hiring:** This is a **composite supply** of service; the transportation is ancillary to the renting. The rate applicable is **12%**.
d664bbb697720e4e5cb147c9c33fa775ca70d5f3:
Yes, Dhruv Kumar qualifies as an agent under Para 3 of Schedule I of the CGST Act, 2017. 

According to the definition of "Agent" provided in Section 2(5) of the CGST Act, a person who carries on the business of supply or receipt of goods or services on behalf of another is an agent. Crucially, the Explanation to Rule 55 of the CGST Rules, 2017, clarifies that a factor, including an auctioneer, who issues an invoice in his own name on behalf of the principal, falls within the scope of an agent. 

Since Dhruv Kumar issues the invoice in his own name for the supply of paintings on behalf of Chandragupta Maurya, he satisfies the criteria of an agent under Para 3 of Schedule I.

Under Section 10(2A) of the CGST Act, 2017, read with Notification No. 2/2019-Central Tax (Rate), a registered person whose aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year did not exceed ₹50 lakh may opt to pay tax at 6% (3% CGST + 3% SGST). fd2d0fa23a22fe335c59f686d95b07132a381012:
The firm is **not eligible** to opt for the composition scheme under **Section 10(2A)** of the CGST Act, 2017. 

As per the eligibility criteria, the scheme is restricted to suppliers of services (or mixed suppliers) whose aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year did not exceed ₹50 lakh. Furthermore, **Section 10(2)(a)** explicitly excludes persons engaged in the supply of services other than those referred to in clause (b) of paragraph 6 of Schedule II (restaurant services). Since the firm provides audit services, it is ineligible for the composition levy.

Consequently, the firm must pay tax at the applicable GST rates on its taxable supplies. There is no concessional tax liability; the firm is liable to pay tax on its entire turnover.

**Place of Supply and Taxability under GST**

As per **Section 13(2) of the IGST Act, 2017**, the place of supply of services, except where the location of the supplier or recipient is outside India, is the location of the recipient of services. Since the recipient (XY Ltd.) is located in Rajasthan, India, the place of supply is Rajasthan.

Under **Section 5(3) of the IGST Act, 2017** read with **Notification No. 10/2017-Integrated Tax (Rate)**, services provided by a person located in a non-taxable territory to a person located in the taxable territory are subject to tax under the **Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM)**. Consequently, XY Ltd. is liable to pay IGST on the consideration of £8,000 under RCM, as it is the recipient of the legal services.

54d3e460b1320386d258c0e616a69e74df1e7355:
The stand taken by the Department is incorrect. As per **Circular No. 32/6/2018-GST**, services provided by senior doctors/consultants/technicians hired by hospitals are considered "health care services" and are exempt under **Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate)**. The hospital acts as a facilitator, and the doctors are essentially providing health care services to the patients. 

Furthermore, the "retention money" retained by the hospital is part of the composite supply of health care services provided to in-patients. Since health care services are exempt, the entire amount charged by the hospital to in-patients, including the retention money for ancillary services (nursing, infrastructure, etc.), is exempt from GST. The hospital is not providing a separate taxable service to the doctors.

As per **Section 12(2) of the CGST Act, 2017**, where the goods are supplied under a contract providing for periodic statements of account or periodic payments, the time of supply shall be the date on which the statement of account is issued or the date on which the payment is received, whichever is earlier.

In the given case, the statement of account for the quarter July–September was issued on **October 3**. The balance payment of ₹56,000 was received on **October 17**. Since the statement of account (October 3) is earlier than the receipt of payment (October 17), the time of supply for the differential amount of ₹56,000 is **October 3**. For the monthly payments already received, the time of supply is the date of receipt.
7ce5c7df22c664ff1b4b315ad7faed17ed7891fa:
As per **Section 13(3) of the CGST Act, 2017**, in case of services received from an associated enterprise located outside India, the time of supply is the earlier of:
(a) The date of entry in the books of account of the recipient; or
(b) The date of payment.

**Case I: Payment on 22nd September**
The date of entry in the books (self-invoice date) is 28th August, and the date of payment is 22nd September. Since 28th August is earlier, the time of supply is **28th August**.

**Case II: Payment on 27th August**
The date of entry in the books is 28th August, and the date of payment is 27th August. Since 27th August is earlier, the time of supply is **27th August**.

**Time of Supply Determination:**

1. **Printing of Books:** As the content is supplied by the author, this constitutes a "supply of goods" (composite supply). Under **Section 12(2)(a) of the CGST Act, 2017**, the time of supply is the earlier of the date of issue of invoice (15th May) or the last date on which the invoice is required to be issued under **Section 31** (13th May, date of removal). Thus, the time of supply is **13th May**.

2. **Printing of Envelopes:** As the design/logo is supplied by the buyer, this is a "supply of services" under **Schedule II**. 8142277ab9485c32a7c8e28f1ecb440c1b058b98:
**Time of Supply Determination:**

**1. Product 'A' (Forward Charge):**
As per **Section 12(2) of the CGST Act, 2017**, the time of supply of goods is the date of issue of invoice or the last date on which the invoice is required to be issued under Section 31. Per **Notification No. 66/2017-Central Tax**, the requirement to pay tax on advances received for the supply of goods is exempted. Thus, the time of supply is the date of invoice issuance, i.e., **4th March**.

**2. Product 'B' (Reverse Charge):**
As per **Section 12(3) of the CGST Act, 2017**, the time of supply is the earliest of: (a) date of receipt of goods, (b) date of payment, or (c) date immediately following 30 days from the date of issue of invoice. Here, the earliest date is the receipt of goods, i.e., **23rd March**.

9ff4a9ade455d857414bd899e3555ae2d2ed8ae2:
Under the GST law, the supply of 'Buy One Get Two Free' is classified as a "supply of goods with more than one individual price" or a "mixed supply" depending on the nature of the offer. 

As per **Section 17(2)** of the **CGST Act, 2017**, read with **Section 16(1)**, a registered person is entitled to take Input Tax Credit (ITC) on inward supplies used in the course or furtherance of business. Since the "free" items are part of a promotional scheme to boost taxable outward supplies, they are considered business-related. Furthermore, **Section 17(5)(h)**, which restricts ITC on goods disposed of by way of gift or free samples, is not applicable here as the items are supplied as part of a commercial transaction, not as gifts. Thus, ITC is fully available.

As per **Section 18(6)** of the CGST Act, 2017, where capital goods on which input tax credit (ITC) has been taken are supplied, the registered person shall pay an amount equal to the ITC taken on the said capital goods reduced by the percentage points as prescribed in **Rule 44(6)**, or the tax on the transaction value of such capital goods, whichever is higher.

1. **ITC Taken:** ₹ 12,39,000 × 18/118 = ₹ 1,89,000.
2. **Reduction:** Usage is 1 year (4 quarters). Reduction = 5% per quarter = 20%. ITC to be reversed = ₹ 1,89,000 - 20% = ₹ 1,51,200.
3. **Tax on Transaction Value:** ₹ 7,50,000 × 18% = ₹ 1,35,000.

Since ₹ 1,51,200 > ₹ 1,35,000, M/s Agarwal & Agarwal must pay **₹ 1,51,200** as GST.

4bdae2d8a20298d1eb360a42e51dd00d1e0d1d55:
As per **Section 20 of the CGST Act, 2017** read with **Rule 39 of the CGST Rules, 2017**, an Input Service Distributor (ISD) must distribute credit in the manner prescribed.

1. **Specific Credit:** Credit attributable to a specific recipient must be distributed only to that recipient.
2. **Common Credit:** Common credit is distributed pro-rata based on the turnover of the recipient in the preceding financial year (or last quarter, if applicable) in a State/UT to the aggregate turnover of all recipients.
3. **Exempted Supplies:** As per Rule 39(1)(d), credit attributable to recipients engaged exclusively in exempted supplies is not distributed. Thus, Madhugiri branch is excluded.
4. **Time Limit:** The IGST of ₹10,000 from last year is time-barred under **Section 16(4)** and cannot be distributed.

2. **Common Credit (Tc):** Includes ITC on Machinery 'U' (₹36,000), Machinery 'Z' (₹54,000), and Machinery 'Y' (proportionate).
3. **Attributable to Exempt Supplies (Te):** Calculated as (Exempt Turnover / Total Turnover) × Tc. Total turnover = ₹25,00,000; Exempt turnover (Beta) = ₹10,00,000. Ratio = 0.4.
4. **Liability:** Output tax on Alpha (₹1,62,000) and Gama (₹1,08,000) minus eligible ITC.

**Calculations:**
(i) ₹1,35,000 (ii) ₹90,000 (iii) ₹36,000 (iv) ₹63,000.

**A. ITC Credited to Electronic Credit Ledger:**
ITC is available on taxable inputs (₹55,00,000 × 18% = ₹9,90,000) and GTA services (₹1,00,000 × 5% = ₹5,000). ITC on exempted/non-taxable inputs, personal rent (Section 17(1)), personal GST (Section 17(5)(g)), rent-a-cab (Section 17(5)(b)), and free samples (Section 17(5)(h)) is blocked. Total ITC = ₹9,95,000.

**B. Common Credit:**
Common credit pertains to input services used for both taxable and exempt supplies. Here, the packing service (₹2,50,000 × 18% = ₹45,000) is common.

**C. ITC Attributable to Exempt Supplies:**
As per Rule 42, common credit is apportioned based on turnover. Exempt turnover = ₹12,00,000 (exempt) + ₹3,00,000 (non-taxable) = ₹15,00,000. Total turnover = ₹42,00,000 + ₹15,00,000 + ₹8,00,000 = ₹65,00,000.
Attributable ITC = ₹45,000 × (15/65) = ₹10,385.

**D. Eligible ITC out of Common Credit:**
₹45,000 - ₹10,385 = ₹34,615.

**E. Net GST Payable:**
Output Tax = (₹42L + ₹8L) × 18% = ₹9,00,000.
Net ITC = ₹9,95,000 - ₹10,385 = ₹9,84,615.
Since ITC exceeds output tax, Net GST payable = Nil.

**(a) Registration Requirement:**
As per Section 22 of the CGST Act, 2017, a person is liable to register if their aggregate turnover exceeds the threshold limit (₹20 lakh for Tamil Nadu). However, Section 23(1)(a) provides that persons exclusively engaged in the business of supplying goods or services that are not liable to tax or are wholly exempt from tax are not liable to registration. Since SNP Pvt. Ltd. exclusively manufactured exempt product 'Z', it was not liable for registration. Upon the withdrawal of the exemption on 1st November, the company becomes a taxable person and must obtain registration under Section 22 if its aggregate turnover exceeds the threshold.

**(b) Input Tax Credit (ITC):**
Under Section 18(1)(c), a registered person who ceases to pay tax under an exemption notification may take credit of input tax in respect of capital goods held on the day immediately preceding the date from which they become liable to pay tax. Credit is reduced by 5 percentage points per quarter or part thereof from the date of the invoice. Since the machinery was purchased on 1st July and the exemption was withdrawn on 1st November, the credit is available after applying the prescribed reduction for the intervening period.

**Analysis:**
1. **Aggregate Turnover:** Under Section 2(6), "aggregate turnover" includes all taxable supplies, exempt supplies, and exports, but excludes inward supplies taxed under reverse charge.
2. **Treatment of Items:**
   - Restaurant services and packed food are taxable supplies.

3. **Threshold Calculation:**

   - March: ₹13,50,000 (6.5L + 2L + 5L)
   - Total: ₹20,50,000.

(a) Yes, an e-way bill is mandatorily required. Under **Rule 138(1) of the CGST Rules, 2017**, an e-way bill must be generated prior to the commencement of movement of goods where the consignment value exceeds ₹50,000. Since the value is ₹48,000 plus 18% GST (₹8,640), the total consignment value is ₹56,640, exceeding the threshold.

(b) As per **Rule 138(1)**, the registered person causing the movement of goods (the consignor) is responsible for generating the e-way bill.

(c) Non-issuance of an e-way bill constitutes a contravention of the provisions of the CGST Act. Under **Section 122(1)(xiv)**, the offender is liable to a penalty of ₹10,000 or the tax sought to be evaded, whichever is higher. Additionally, **Section 129** empowers authorities to detain or seize the goods and conveyance.

Under the provisions of **Section 49(10) of the CGST Act, 2017**, read with **Rule 87(13) of the CGST Rules, 2017**, a registered person may transfer any amount of tax, interest, penalty, fee, or any other amount available in the electronic cash ledger to the electronic cash ledger for IGST, CGST, or SGST/UTGST in **Form GST PMT-09**.

However, this facility is strictly limited to the **Electronic Cash Ledger**. Input Tax Credit (ITC) is maintained in the **Electronic Credit Ledger**. As per the law, ITC cannot be transferred between heads (IGST to CGST/SGST) via Form GST PMT-09. Mr. X must reverse the wrongly availed ITC and re-avail the correct credit, subject to the conditions prescribed under **Section 16** and **Section 17** of the CGST Act.

As per **Rule 86(4B)(a)** of the CGST Rules, 2017, where a refund claim filed under **Section 54** of the CGST Act, 2017, in respect of zero-rated supply of goods made without payment of tax is rejected, the amount debited from the Electronic Credit Ledger to the extent of such rejection shall be re-credited to the ledger by the proper officer by an order made in **Form GST PMT-03**.

In the case of M/s Neptune & Co., since the refund of ₹ 10,14,000 was rejected, Mr. A is legally entitled to seek the re-credit of the said amount. The proper officer is mandated to issue an order in Form GST PMT-03 to restore the credit in the Electronic Credit Ledger, provided the rejection order has attained finality.

Under Section 51 of the CGST Act, 2017, read with Notification No. 50/2018-Central Tax, TDS at 2% (1% CGST + 1% SGST or 2% IGST) is deductible only if the total value of supply under a contract exceeds ₹2,50,000.

**TDS Applicability:**
(i) ₹15,000: No (Contract < ₹2.5L).
(ii) ₹20,000: Yes (Contract > ₹2.5L); TDS: ₹400.
(iii) ₹25,000: Yes (Contract > ₹2.5L); TDS: ₹500.
(iv) ₹50,000: Yes (Contract > ₹2.5L); TDS: ₹1,000.
(v) ₹12,39,000: Yes (Contract > ₹2.5L); TDS: ₹24,780.
(vi) ₹20,000 (Taxable portion): Yes (Contract > ₹2.5L); TDS: ₹400.
(vii) ₹3,50,000: No (Exempt under Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax as a function under Article 243W).

**Composition Scheme:** TDS provisions under Section 51 remain applicable regardless of the supplier's registration scheme.

Yes, GST Practitioners (GSTPs) are required to furnish a statement of activities. Under **Section 48** of the CGST Act, 2017, read with **Rule 83(8)** of the CGST Rules, 2017, every GSTP must prepare a monthly statement of the particulars of all statements and returns furnished by them on behalf of registered persons.

This statement must be furnished in **Form GST PCT-07** electronically on the common portal. The statement must be filed for every calendar month by the **10th day of the succeeding month**. This requirement ensures transparency and accountability regarding the professional services rendered by the GSTP. Failure to comply with these procedural requirements may lead to the cancellation of the GSTP’s enrollment under Rule 83A.
